# Shell that MUST be refused — the other half of the guard corpus (see shell_corpus.txt).
#
# Format: `<command><TAB><expected reason prefix>`; `#` lines are comments; `\n` decodes to a
# newline. The prefix is what GitArchaeologyGuard.check_shell must START with:
#   archaeology:  reaches another revision, history, the shared stash stack or `.git`
#   network:      leaves the sandbox (fetch / install / registry / cloud)
# Nothing here is a matter of taste: every line either recovers the real patch, reaches
# the network, mutates the provisioned environment, or cannot be parsed safely (fail-closed).
#
# NOT here on purpose: shell edits to TEST files (`sed -i … foo_test.go`, `> tests/x.py`).
# The shell guard is path-blind and cannot classify tests; belt 1 (TestFileGuard.tampered /
# Workspace.tests_byte_identical) catches every such edit post hoc, byte for byte, however it
# was made. See test_builders_guard_corpus.py::test_shell_edits_to_tests_are_belt_1.
